items.review_rationale: Reviewed full additive and multiplicative preservation identities of a map between associative, possibly nonunital rings; identified the function and ring prerequisites without imposing unit preservation.

references.context: Binary ring addition and compatibility of the mapping with addition for all a,b in its domain.
Compatibility of the same mapping with associative ring multiplication for all a,b in its domain.
Ring identities may exist, but preservation is not part of this nonunital homomorphism definition.

references.disposition: The absence of phi(1_R)=1_S is a scope distinction, not an additional condition.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed full unital ring-homomorphism formulation, separating the additive and multiplicative preservation inherited from the nonunital meaning from the additional preservation of specified units.

references.phrase: unital associative rings R and S

references.context: Two-sided multiplicative identity elements in the source and target rings.
Extra condition distinguishing a unital ring homomorphism from the unrestricted ring-homomorphism meaning.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed complete sigma-algebra axioms on an underlying set, recording power set, relative complement and countable union separately and distinguishing the positive-integer indexing convention.

references.context: Set of all subsets of an underlying set X, serving as the ambient collection for Sigma.
Set complement of a member A of Sigma relative to X.
Union of a sequence of members of Sigma indexed by positive integers, with closure of Sigma under that union.

references.disposition: The requirement X belongs to the family Sigma is an axiom of the definition, not a claim that Sigma contains every subset.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed alternative sigma-algebra axiomatization through set differences and countable pairwise-disjoint unions, without treating it as an independently new meaning or assuming arbitrary countable unions as a primitive.

references.context: Collection of all subsets of X in which the sigma-algebra Sigma is a family.
Relative set difference for two members A,B of Sigma.
A sequence of sets whose members have empty intersection whenever their indices differ.

references.phrase: countable union of pairwise disjoint members
references.context: Closure under unions of all members of any countably indexed pairwise disjoint sequence in Sigma.

references.disposition: The ambient-set membership condition is an axiom; the equivalent formulation need not list arbitrary countable-union closure explicitly.
These are alternative closure axioms defining the same sigma-algebra concept, not an additional dependency on itself.
